NDT training in Pueblo, CO: how it works in a steel and rail town

Short answer: NDT training for Pueblo technicians and employers combines self-paced online theory on the Atlantis portal, questions answered by an ASNT NDT Level III, practice in the Practical NDT browser simulator, and hands-on work and examinations at the employer's own mill, shop or plant. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Pueblo. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and the employer signs the certification. We reply within one business day.

Pueblo has made steel for well over a century, and the work that grew around the mill still defines the city: rail, heavy plate, structural fabrication, power generation and the equipment that keeps them running. Most of that work is welded or rolled carbon steel, which is why visual, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing do the heavy lifting here, with radiography on pressure piping and penetrant on the occasional stainless or non-magnetic part.

It is also a city where an inspection technician can find steady work without moving to Denver. Mill maintenance, tower fabrication, power-plant outages, railcar repair and pipeline jobs across the Arkansas Valley all need people who can follow a procedure, find a crack and write it up properly.

Request a Pueblo training quote with the methods, levels and number of people you need. Useful background: the NDT training FAQ, the training catalogue and the US training overview.

How to get NDT certified in Pueblo: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

There is no state NDT licence in Colorado. Certification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A is issued by the employer against its own written practice, which spells out the hours, examinations and vision rules for each method and level. The sequence for a Pueblo technician:

  1. Find a sponsoring employer. Its written practice needs to cover the method and level you want. In Pueblo, plenty of technicians move into NDT from welding, millwright or quality roles inside the same company.
  2. Complete the required training hours. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method; your employer may set higher numbers.
  3. Gain supervised experience performing the method under a certified Level II or Level III, and log every hour.
  4. Pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment and acceptance criteria, such as AWS D1.1 for structural welds or the customer specification for tower seams.
  6. Pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or an examiner under one.
  7. Pass the vision examination covering near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated as the written practice requires. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker walks through it.
  8. Receive certification signed by the employer.
  9. Recertify on schedule; SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years between certifications.

If you want a credential that stays with you rather than with one company, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and the ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative, and Atlantis prepares candidates for it. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Pueblo technicians

Level 1 courses teach what a technician needs to carry out examinations under supervision. Level 2 courses add set-up, calibration, evaluation against acceptance criteria and reporting. Level III preparation is for experienced technicians heading toward the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and the job of writing procedures.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Pueblo, and the magnetic particle work around it

Ultrasonic testing in Pueblo is mostly about thick steel. Wind-tower sections are rolled from heavy plate and joined with long seam welds and flange welds that are examined ultrasonically to the turbine maker's specification. Rail and wheelsets are checked for internal flaws. At power-plant outages, technicians take thickness readings on boiler tubes and piping and examine welds. The ultrasonic testing training course covers the physics, calibration on reference blocks, straight-beam and angle-beam technique, sizing basics and the reporting that lets an engineer make a decision. Test your theory with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Magnetic particle testing sits right beside UT on almost every Pueblo job, because it is fast and effective on carbon steel. A good MT course goes beyond pressing a yoke to the steel: it covers field direction and why two perpendicular shots are needed, surface preparation on mill scale and paint, wet fluorescent technique, and how to tell a relevant indication from a geometric one.

Where NDT technicians work around Pueblo

Steel and rail. Rocky Mountain Steel Mills became part of Orion Steel when Atlas Holdings completed its purchase of EVRAZ North America in 2025. The Pueblo mill is a major producer of rail for North American railroads and draws much of its power from a dedicated solar facility. Mill operations, maintenance and the contractors that support them need MT, UT and VT on equipment, repairs and product.

Wind-tower fabrication. The large wind-tower plant on the south side of the city, built by Vestas and acquired by CS Wind, rolls and welds tower sections from heavy plate. Long seam welds and flange welds make this one of the more UT- and MT-intensive manufacturing jobs in the state, with weld visual on every section.

Power generation. Xcel Energy's Comanche Generating Station south of the city brings outage work: boiler tube thickness surveys, weld examination on piping and headers, and MT and PT on rotating equipment. Boiler and power piping work follows ASME practice and National Board rules for repairs.

Rail testing and repair. The federally owned Transportation Technology Center northeast of Pueblo tests rail vehicles, track and components, and railcar repair and rail maintenance contractors work throughout southern Colorado. Wheel, axle and component inspection follows railroad and AAR requirements set by the customer.

Pipelines, cement and construction. Natural gas transmission lines cross the Arkansas Valley, cement plants operate in Pueblo and Fremont counties, and bridge, building and industrial steel across the region is inspected to AWS D1.1 and D1.5. Pueblo is a welding town, so for anyone heading toward weld inspection, Atlantis also offers a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course; AWS administers the exam and issues the certification.

The I-25 corridor. Colorado Springs, forty-odd miles north, adds aerospace, defence and utility work, and many Pueblo technicians commute or travel up the interstate for outages and projects. For wages, see the NDT salary guide, which cites public sources.

NDT schools and classes near Pueblo: what to compare

Search "ndt classes Pueblo" or "ndt school near me" and you will mostly find welding programmes locally and NDT-specific providers further north along the Front Range. Pueblo Community College runs a welding programme with an associate degree and certificates for structural, high-pressure pipe and low-pressure pipe welding, on its Pueblo and Fremont campuses among others; it gives a strong grounding in how welds are made, which helps anyone moving into inspection. Dedicated NDT courses with set timetables are mostly found around Denver. Self-paced online providers, Atlantis among them, put the theory online and leave the practical to the employer.

Which suits you depends on your situation. A person with no job yet may want a structured programme with lab time. A welder or millwright already employed in Pueblo usually wants theory that fits around shifts and a practical examination done on the employer's own equipment and parts.

Ask any provider these questions before you pay:

  • Will the training hours count under the written practice of the employer you want to work for?
  • Who grades the practical examination, and is that person a Level III in the method?
  • Does the course cover the codes local employers use, such as AWS D1.1 and ASME practice?
  • Is the provider clear that the employer certifies, not the course?
  • Can you go back to the material later, when you prepare for Level II?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Pueblo and does not pretend to. What it provides is online theory with Level III support, simulator practice, and the practical and examinations at the sponsoring employer's facility. If you still need a sponsor, the near-me guide suggests how to ask a Pueblo shop to take you on.

Online NDT training in Colorado

Colorado technicians can complete Level I and Level II theory online on the Atlantis portal, and Level III candidates can prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations the same way. Access opens the moment you enrol, courses run year-round, and the Level III answers questions as you go. That suits mill workers on rotating shifts, outage crews who travel, and anyone in the San Luis Valley or the plains east of Pueblo far from a training provider. The practical training and examination are hands-on with the employer. More on the online NDT training page and the Colorado training page.

A quick question to your employer's Level III before you enrol, about how many online classroom hours the written practice accepts, avoids surprises later.

Training a crew at your Pueblo facility

A Pueblo fabricator, mill contractor or utility qualifying several people can keep production going: theory is studied online, and the specific and practical examinations are held at your shop on your instruments and specimens cut from your own work. For a tower or structural fabricator, that means the practical examination uses the weld joints and thicknesses your crew actually inspects. Outage contractors can have new hires examined before the season starts, so they arrive on site already certified.

If your written practice is out of date, or you are adding a method, our Level III can help. See written practice development, corporate NDT training and outsourced Level III consulting, or ask about training a Pueblo crew.

Radiography licensing in Colorado

Colorado is an NRC Agreement State, and the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment regulates radioactive materials, including the sources used for industrial radiography. A company radiographing pipe or boiler welds in Pueblo County needs that licence, and its radiographers must meet the training, examination and supervision requirements in the licence and state regulations. An RT course teaches exposure technique and interpretation under SNT-TC-1A, but it licenses nobody and gives no authority to handle a source. Most radiographers therefore hold two qualifications: state-driven radiation safety credentials and an employer's RT certification. Confirm the current requirements with the department.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets Pueblo trainees rehearse set-ups, scan coverage and interpretation between hands-on sessions; the welding workshop and the magnetic particle simulator suit fabrication work. The NDT practice tests check general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools, not a substitute for hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

The courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, founder of Atlantis NDT, an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT with more than eleven years of international field experience. He authors the course material, oversees examinations and reviews employers' written practices and procedures.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Pueblo

How do I become an NDT technician in Colorado?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training hours and supervised experience it sets, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Atlantis covers the online theory, the exam preparation and the Level III questions along the way.

Is there an NDT school in Pueblo?

Pueblo Community College teaches welding, which is useful groundwork, and dedicated NDT courses are mostly found around Denver. Atlantis has no building in Pueblo; theory is online and the practical takes place at an employer's facility.

What is the best first NDT method for a Pueblo welder?

Visual testing, then magnetic particle. Both build directly on what a welder already knows about weld defects. Ultrasonic testing is the usual next step.

Can I study NDT online in Colorado?

Yes, for theory. Every Level I and II module, and the Level III preparation, can be studied online from anywhere in the state. The practical training and the practical examination are done hands-on with an employer.

Are there NDT jobs in Pueblo?

Steel, wind-tower fabrication, power generation, rail and pipeline work all employ inspectors or hire inspection contractors. Check employers' and contractors' postings for their entry requirements.

How long does UT Level 2 take?

The written practice decides. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours, and the experience log usually takes the longest. See the training-requirements matrix.

What does NDT training cost in Pueblo?

The published US fees for the standard courses are listed in the table on this page. Onsite programmes for a group are quoted once we know the methods, levels and numbers.

If I leave the mill for a contractor, is my certification still valid?

Not by itself. The contractor reviews your training, experience and examination records and certifies you under its own written practice. ASNT central certification is the portable option.

Can I prepare for Level III from Pueblo?

Yes. The Level III preparation runs online at your own pace, and a Level III answers your questions. See ASNT Level III training.

Which nearby cities have training guides?

Colorado Springs, Denver, Albuquerque, Wichita and Salt Lake City each have their own page.
